name: SVAMITVA Drone Aerial Imagery (Kaggle community mirror)
source: Kaggle community dataset published by user 'utkarshsaxenadn' (display name DeepNets). Imagery origin: drone imagery supplied by the Smart India Hackathon from the SVAMITVA scheme (Survey of India / Ministry of Panchayati Raj).
geography: India - SVAMITVA village drone survey imagery. The publisher does not enumerate the specific villages, districts or states included, so the exact geographic footprint is UNDECLARED. Locally verified: the publisher's own tiffTopatches.py patchifies ONE source raster ('suragpur.tif') with patchify(step=1024), so every tile in this download originates from a single survey, not a nationwide sample.
date: 2025-01 (Kaggle publication date; underlying imagery from SVAMITVA / Smart India Hackathon 2024-2025)
resolution: Imagery split into 1024x1024 px patches. Ground sample distance is not declared by the publisher. Total published size ~7.30 GB. Locally verified: 1322 image/mask pairs used for training; images are 1024x1024 RGBA PNG and masks are 1024x1024 RGB PNG (or RGBA for the binary variant).
crs: Not declared by the publisher. Patches are supplied without geo-referencing metadata, so they cannot be placed in a cadastral CRS frame. The 4 bulk TestGeoTiff rasters in the download are geo-referenced but carry NO masks and were deliberately not used.
labels: RGB CLASS-COLOURED building masks, not binary images. Verified locally against the publisher's own poly2mask.py: Building = (0,110,255), Field = (85,217,48), Road = (255,0,0), Water = (0,238,255), Other = (200,255,0), background = (0,0,0). An independent colour census across all 1322 masks found exactly these six colours, with Building covering 18.38% of annotated pixels overall. Building-positive tiles: 690/1322 (52.2%), matching the 690 files in the publisher's FilteredData folder exactly. Labels therefore require an EXACT COLOUR MATCH; binarising with 'pixel > 0' would mislabel Field, Road, Water and Other as building. These masks are COMMUNITY-ANNOTATED, NOT Survey of India ground truth.
license: CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication), as declared on the Kaggle dataset page.
provenance: Obtained from Kaggle behind an authenticated Kaggle account and API token; not an official data.gov.in or state portal publication. Processing chain performed by the publisher: original ECW imagery converted to TIF with QGIS/GDAL, tiled to 1024x1024 patches, then annotated. Used ONLY as the last-resort training source approved on 2026-09-23; every checkpoint trained on it records dataset_provenance=KAGGLE_BENCHMARK together with this manifest. The third-party pretrained models bundled in the dataset are NOT used: this repository trains its own U-Net from scratch. Integrity was verified after download (4,785,147,343 bytes, zip integrity OK, 4,731 entries).
limitations: Real government-origin drone imagery carrying third-party community annotations. This is NOT an official government publication and NOT authoritative cadastral ground truth. The publisher states the annotations were completed within a single day and may contain inaccuracies. No CRS or geo-referencing is supplied, so spatial independence of tiles CANNOT be verified from metadata. Audited locally, four further limitations matter: (1) FilteredData is a strict SUBSET of Full Data - its 690 names are contained in Full Data's 1322 and its patch_1.png is byte-identical, so combining the folders would double-count 690 tiles; (2) FilteredData/BinaryMasks is NOT a clean binary label image - it is a matplotlib viridis-colormapped render containing exactly two distinct pixel values, (68,1,84) and (253,231,36), and would poison training if paired as a mask; (3) 61 tiles (4.6%) are nodata padding with mean brightness < 10, 41 of them >99% near-black, concentrated in the low-index region - these are excluded rather than labelled 'no building'; (4) consecutive patch indices share pixel seams (mean edge difference 31.5 at lag 1 versus a 51.0 random-pair baseline), so tiles are SPATIALLY ADJACENT, meaning a random tile split leaks near-identical neighbours; tile order is also not density-neutral (positive rate 20-58% across deciles 0-6 rising to 78-100% across deciles 7-9). Geographic coverage is undeclared, so the sample cannot be treated as representative of any state or district. Prohibited as an active training source by ml-engine/AGENTS.md section 3 (Kaggle); it is used only under the dated amendment recorded in that section.
intended_use: Task 1 - Building Footprint Extraction: training, validation and test. Primary evaluation uses a CONTIGUOUS, spatially-disjoint split of tile order because only one survey is present and no scene grouping exists; this avoids neighbour leakage but carries a measured building-density shift between splits, which is reported per split rather than corrected. A stratified random split is additionally reported, explicitly labelled leakage-optimistic. Must always be reported with KAGGLE_BENCHMARK provenance. Must never be presented as data.gov.in-compliant, as authoritative cadastral truth, or as a validated pan-India model. Height, floor-count and unit targets are NOT supported by this dataset.
